solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Speak out against a game getting commercial

parts.note: nim is a game in which players take turns removing objects from heaps
a commercial on TV is an advert

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a sports fixture or contest being taken over by advertising money.
explanation.definitionFit: To animadvert is a formal verb meaning to criticise or pass censure on something.

clue.text: Retreat as sheep hiding under tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece sheltering under another is written below it, so it comes second

parts.note: the ash is a common tree
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A flock shelters beneath a tree, as sheep do from rain or sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is only a joining word here; 'hiding under' places the sheep below the tree in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a religious hermitage in India, a place of spiritual retreat.

clue.text: Somewhere to drink at home before start of great American sports session?

parts.note: an inn is a pub, a place for a drink
someone at home is 'in'

indicators.note: start of means only the opening letter of the word great is used

explanation.surface: A drinker settles in at the pub at home before watching a big American game.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the end of the clue: in American baseball an inning is one team's turn at bat.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball each of the nine periods of play is called an inning, the US form of the cricket word innings.

clue.text: Unpredictability of starer — brain is addled

indicators.note: addled means muddled or confused, so the letters are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who stares vacantly has a confused mind and acts unpredictably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like a link word but belongs to the anagram fodder with STARER and BRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Arbitrariness is the quality of acting on whim rather than rule, hence being unpredictable.

clue.text: Best veal, minced say for eating — served with such?

definitions.text: Best veal, minced say for eating — served with such?

indicators.note: for eating means the shuffled meat swallows the other piece
minced meat is chopped up, so these letters are chopped and rearranged

parts.note: say introduces an example, abbreviated as eg

explanation.surface: A cook prepares fine minced veal and wonders what side dishes should go with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minced' turns BEST VEAL into VETABLES, and 'for eating' puts EG inside it after VE; the whole clue then hints at what accompanies the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Greens and potatoes are the usual side dishes served alongside a meat course.

clue.text: This part makes audible rumble

indicators.note: makes audible tells us to take a word as spoken, matching its pronunciation not spelling

parts.note: a rumble of thunder or drums is a roll

explanation.surface: An actor's piece of the script includes a loud rumbling noise.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's part in a play or film is also called the character they play.

clue.text: It's not quite right ditching a girl

indicators.note: ditching means dropping, so the named letter is removed

parts.note: something amiss is wrong or not quite right

explanation.surface: Someone admits it was wrong to dump a girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a joining phrase; dropping A from the front of AMISS leaves the young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss is a title for, and an old word for, a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Bother with slowing down — get cross about that

indicators.note: about means going round, so the angry word encloses the musical term

parts.note: cross means angry, irate
rit, short for ritardando, is the musical direction for slowing down

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed by a vehicle slowing down ahead and gets angry about it.
explanation.walkthrough: RIT is the musical abbreviation of ritardando; it sits after the IR of IRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To bother someone is to annoy them, a straightforward synonym for vex.

clue.text: Chemical is held up after being shaken

indicators.note: something shaken has its contents jumbled, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chemical sample is lifted up for inspection after being shaken in its flask.
explanation.definitionFit: A sulphide is a chemical compound of sulphur with another element.

clue.text: Compact container?

parts.note: reads as a small neat box, but a compact is a powder case that a woman's bag holds

explanation.surface: Something small and neat for storing things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compact' seems an adjective; it is the noun, a make-up powder case.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's purse-style bag typically carries her powder compact among other items.

clue.text: Old-fashioned politician, I'll bear being beaten

indicators.note: beaten as eggs are whisked, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A traditional politician resigns himself to losing the election.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberal Party was a major British party before merging into the Liberal Democrats in 1988, hence 'old-fashioned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the former British Liberal Party, now historical, were Liberals.

clue.text: Dr's been mean, I'd fancy — one needing to develop this sympathetic approach?

indicators.note: fancy as a verb meaning imagine; as an adjective it means elaborate, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient thinks the doctor has been unkind, and that he needs to work on his manner with patients.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of Dr's is part of the fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's way with patients, especially kindness and tact, is the classic idiom for a gentle sympathetic manner.

clue.text: Comment on Queen carrying old rubbish

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the monarch's name surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: Anne was a Queen of Great Britain
tat is cheap worthless goods

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on a monarch hauling around a load of old junk.
explanation.definitionFit: To annotate a text is to add notes or remarks to it.

clue.text: Get rid of daughter, cause of irritation

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family records
an itch is something that irritates the skin

explanation.surface: An exasperated parent wants to be free of a daughter who is a constant annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: To dump or discard something is to abandon it, as a ship ditched at sea.

clue.text: One in reality TV sadly demonstrates an absence of fixed standards

indicators.note: sadly here hints at things gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Reality television shows that its participants have no fixed moral standards.
explanation.definitionFit: Relativism, the view that truth and morals are not absolute but depend on context, is described this way.

clue.text: Reduced to a bare minimum, like BBC?

definitions.meaning: BBC is the short form of British Broadcasting Corporation, a set of initials

explanation.surface: The BBC cut back to a skeleton service.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortened words or phrases, like initials for a long name, are cut-down forms.

clue.text: Withering grass outside animal hospital

indicators.note: outside means placed around, so the informer's word surrounds the others

parts.note: to grass is slang for informing to the police, as is to sing
a cat is an animal
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Dried-up grass grows around the outside of a veterinary clinic.
explanation.definitionFit: A withering look or remark is cutting and contemptuous, as is a harsh critical one.

clue.text: Church member's point of view, briefly an assertion of personal ability

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an angle is a viewpoint on a story
saying 'I can' asserts that you are able

explanation.surface: A churchgoer's opinion, summed up, is a confident claim of being able to do things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church member's' is 'Church member is'; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the Church of England is a member of the established English church.

clue.text: Heedful opposing team gains speed

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a side is a team in sport
rate means speed, as in rate of knots

explanation.surface: A careful rival team picks up pace during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Being mindful of others' needs is being thoughtful, which is what heedful means here.

clue.text: Little house with B&B — thing to suit fictional adventurer?

parts.note: HO is the short form of house, little meaning abbreviated
the two Bs of bed and breakfast
it can mean a thing

explanation.surface: A small cottage running bed and breakfast seems just right for a storybook traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: Bilbo Baggins is Tolkien's hero; such creatures live in small holes, so the house is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien's Bilbo Baggins, a small hairy-footed halfling, sets out on a quest in his famous novel.

clue.text: Lake I approach going straight from A to B?

definitions.text: going straight from A to B?

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake on maps
to approach is to near

explanation.surface: Someone approaching a lake walks directly from one point to another.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight-line path between two points is one-dimensional, like a line.

clue.text: Fine material — group of workers turned over length of it?

parts.note: TU stands for trade union, a body of workers

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so the word for the measure runs backwards

parts.note: an ell is an old unit of length for cloth

explanation.surface: A union of textile workers rolls over a length of fine fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulle is a fine silk or nylon net used for veils and ballet tutus.

clue.text: Foreign capital with fashionable people having one exotic dish

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia
the ton is an old term for high society
one is written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Smart people in a European capital share a foreign meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridged tube-shaped pasta is an Italian food, so exotic from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: Limited number of musicians in choir turning up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters read from bottom to top
in means the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Only a few singers in a choir show up.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters OIRT run across 'choir turning'; 'up' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Three performers playing together are a group, the smallest after a duo.

clue.text: One possibly cutting and possibly ironic about society

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the abbreviation
possibly means the word could be in another order, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued person might be sardonic and ironic about society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One possibly cutting' suggests a sharp critic but means a tooth; the second 'possibly' rearranges INCIOR around S ('about').
explanation.definitionFit: Front teeth that bite and slice food are the cutting teeth.

clue.text: Base one established north of French city about to be demolished

indicators.note: north of means placed above or before the other piece

parts.note: one is written as the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: demolished means knocked down, so the named part is removed

parts.note: Grenoble is a city in the French Alps
re means about, as in business letters

explanation.surface: A base is set up north of a French city due to be razed.
explanation.definitionFit: Base means low or dishonourable in character, as ignoble does.

clue.text: Energy no good? One makes a noise

parts.note: go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: Someone lacks energy and is useless, but at least makes a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: A gong is a metal disc that is struck to produce a resonant sound.

clue.text: Provider of publicity to plagiarise someone else's work?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, one who copies another author

explanation.surface: An advertising writer stealing another's material.
explanation.definitionFit: Advertising agencies employ writers to craft the text of ads and promotions.
